title: SongManifest
description: The manifest of one song directory. It records which artifacts exist, the content hash of each, and the dependency edges between them, so that any artifact can be re-derived from its recorded inputs and any output can be traced back to the exact prompt, lyrics and composition that produced it. This is what makes the audio a build product rather than an unrepeatable event.

song_seed.description: The single seed every stage derives from. Changing it changes everything downstream; it is recorded here so a whole song is reproducible from one number plus the brief.

artifacts.description: One entry per produced artifact. An absent artifact is a stage that has not run.

role.description: The artifact's place in the pipeline. 'brief' is user input; 'spec', 'composition', 'lyrics', 'prompt' are source artifacts; 'rendered_prompt' is a target-specific projection of prompt; 'audio' and 'stems' are build products; 'report' is the verdict.

seed.description: The stage-local seed actually used, derived from song_seed. Recorded per artifact so one stage can be re-run without perturbing another.

generator.description: For build products, the generator id that produced it.

edges.description: Directed dependencies between artifacts, as (from, to) pairs meaning 'to' was derived from 'from'. This is the regeneration graph: to rebuild one artifact, rebuild it and everything reachable from it.

environment.description: What would have to match for a re-render to be bit-identical. Recorded even though bit-exactness is only best-effort, because the measurement layer can still compare two renders when the bytes differ.

status.description: How far the bundle got. 'partial' means source artifacts exist but no audio; that is a legitimate and useful state, because the prompt, lyrics and composition are reviewable and re-renderable on their own.

parent_manifest_sha256.description: Set when this bundle was derived from an earlier one by changing a single stage, so the lineage of an edit is recoverable.
